hypothesis: A potential hypothesis is that integrating retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) techniques with de novo molecular design could enhance the efficiency and accuracy of generating novel drug-like compounds by leveraging external knowledge bases to inform and refine the design process. RAG models, which combine parametric and non-parametric memory, have demonstrated improved performance in knowledge-intensive tasks by generating more factual and diverse outputs [2005.11401:0][self-rag:0]. Similarly, de novo molecular design benefits from exploring vast chemical spaces and generating candidates from scratch, a process that could be optimized by incorporating relevant external data through RAG methods [denovo-genai-survey:1][denovo-genai-survey:0]. This integration could potentially reduce the time and cost associated with traditional drug discovery methods while improving the quality of generated molecular candidates.
